title: Performance Issues

header.html: 5.4 Given a scenario, troubleshoot common performance issues: congestion and contention; bottlenecking; bandwidth and throughput capacity; latency; packet loss; jitter; wireless issues (interference, channel overlap, signal degradation or loss, insufficient coverage, client disassociation, roaming misconfiguration)
the official CompTIA Network+ N10-009 exam objectives, version 4.0

html:
1Wired performance terms

Term Meaning
Congestion / contention Too much traffic for the link or many devices competing for the same resource; queues fill, packets drop
Bottleneck The slowest point on the path that limits overall speed (a slow uplink, an oversubscribed switch)
Bandwidth The maximum capacity of a link
Throughput The data actually delivered (always at or below the bandwidth)
Latency Delay: time for a packet to travel (ms); high with satellite, distance, congestion
Packet loss Packets that never arrive; causes retransmissions and bad voice and video
Jitter Variation in delay between packets; hurts voice and video (choppy audio)
Exam tip

. Choppy voice and video = jitter, latency or packet loss. Fix with QoS, more bandwidth, or removing the bottleneck. Bandwidth is capacity; throughput is what you actually get.

2Common wired causes and fixes

Cause Fix
Saturated uplink Upgrade the link, add link aggregation, apply QoS
Duplex or speed mismatch Match both ends (auto-negotiate)
Broadcast storm or loop STP, remove the loop
Faulty cable or NIC Replace; check counters
Oversubscription Add capacity or redesign (for example spine and leaf)

3Wireless performance issues

Issue Cause and fix
Interference Other radios (microwave, Bluetooth, neighbor APs), non-Wi-Fi sources; move to 5 GHz or 6 GHz, use a spectrum analyzer
Channel overlap Neighboring APs on overlapping channels; use 1, 6 and 11 at 2.4 GHz
Signal degradation or loss Distance, walls, metal, water; move the AP, raise power, use better antennas
Insufficient coverage Dead spots; add APs after a site survey and heat map
Client disassociation Clients drop off the network: weak signal, too many clients, authentication or power-save problems, channel interference
Roaming misconfiguration Clients cling to a distant AP or drop when moving; same SSID, security and VLAN on all APs, correct power and thresholds, fast roaming (802.11r)
Exam tip

. "Wi-Fi is slow only in one corner" = coverage or signal degradation; check the heat map. "Clients drop when walking between APs" = roaming configuration.

Exam tip

. Jitter and packet loss ruin voice and video; bandwidth is capacity, throughput is what you get.

Exam tip

. Wireless: use channels 1, 6 and 11 at 2.4 GHz; check the heat map for coverage gaps.

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Voice calls are choppy because packet delay varies widely. Which term describes this?

  • ABandwidth
  • BThroughput
  • CJitter
  • DAttenuation
Show the answer

Answer: C. Jitter is variation in delay.

S2A 1 Gbps link delivers only 400 Mbps of useful data. Which statement is correct?

  • AThroughput is lower than the link bandwidth
  • BBandwidth is lower than throughput
  • CLatency is lower than bandwidth
  • DThe jitter is the same as the bandwidth
Show the answer

Answer: A. Throughput is actual delivered data and is at most the bandwidth.

S3Two neighboring APs on channels 3 and 4 cause slow Wi-Fi. What is the best fix?

  • ARaise both to maximum power on the same channels
  • BDisable the 5 GHz radios
  • CSwitch the SSID to ad hoc mode
  • DMove them to non-overlapping channels such as 1 and 6
Show the answer

Answer: D. Non-overlapping channels remove the interference.

S4Users walking between floors lose their video calls as they move between APs. What should be reviewed?

  • AThe DHCP lease time
  • BThe DNS TTL
  • CRoaming configuration on the APs and controller
  • DThe NTP stratum
Show the answer

Answer: C. Roaming misconfiguration drops clients between APs.

S5An upgraded branch is still slow because all traffic funnels through one 100 Mbps uplink. What is this?

  • AA broadcast storm
  • BAn evil twin
  • CA bottleneck
  • DA rogue AP
Show the answer

Answer: C. The slowest link limits overall speed.

S6Wi-Fi is weak only in one corner of the building. What is the best next step?

  • AReplace all switches
  • BReview the wireless heat map and add or move an AP
  • CIncrease the DHCP scope
  • DChange the NTP server
Show the answer

Answer: B. A heat map reveals coverage gaps.

4.2 Recall questions

R1What is the difference between bandwidth and throughput?

Show the answer

Bandwidth is capacity; throughput is the data actually delivered.

R2What does latency measure?

Show the answer

The delay a packet experiences traveling.

R3What is a bottleneck?

Show the answer

The slowest point that limits overall speed.

R4What is client disassociation?

Show the answer

A wireless client dropping off the network.

R5Name two causes of wireless interference.

Show the answer

For example neighboring APs and microwave ovens.

R6What helps voice quality on a congested link?

Show the answer

QoS prioritizing the voice traffic.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Terms bandwidth (capacity), throughput (delivered), latency (delay), jitter (delay variation), packet loss
Wired congestion, bottleneck, duplex mismatch, loops; QoS, upgrades
Wireless interference, channel overlap, signal loss, coverage, disassociation, roaming
Fixes QoS, channels 1/6/11, 5 or 6 GHz, heat map and more APs
